content.value_statement: Real-time voice applications require careful session, audio, and event setup. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for @azure/ai-voicelive.
actual_capabilities: Shows Microsoft Entra ID and API key authentication options.
Guides session setup for modalities, voices, turn detection, and audio formats.
Maps event handlers for connection, transcription, responses, audio, and errors.
Demonstrates function calling flow and browser microphone setup concepts.
limitations: Does not provide a complete runnable application scaffold.
Requires valid Azure AI resources, credentials, and service access.
Uses beta package examples that may change with SDK releases.
Does not test current runtime behavior inside your project.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Voice Assistant
use_cases.description: Create a TypeScript plan for sessions, voices, audio streaming, and response handling.

use_cases.title: Add Voice to Support Workflows
use_cases.description: Design event handlers and function calling for customer service voice interactions.

use_cases.title: Review Azure Voice Integration
use_cases.description: Check authentication, audio formats, turn detection, and cleanup patterns before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the azure-ai-voicelive-ts skill to explain the minimum setup for an Azure AI Voice Live TypeScript project.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the azure-ai-voicelive-ts skill to plan a voice assistant session with audio and text responses.

prompt_templates.title: Design Event Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the azure-ai-voicelive-ts skill to design event handlers for transcription, response audio, errors, and cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the azure-ai-voicelive-ts skill to review my proposed Azure Voice Live architecture for credentials, audio flow, and reliability risks.

output_examples.input: Help me choose Voice Live settings for a customer support assistant.
output: Recommended model: a lightweight real-time model for faster turn taking.
Recommended voice: an Azure standard voice that matches the product locale.
Recommended turn detection: Azure semantic VAD for more natural conversation flow.
Add handlers for connection errors, transcription completion, response audio, and cleanup.

output_examples.input: Review my browser voice assistant plan before I build it.
output: Use browser-compatible authentication and avoid embedding secrets in client code.
Request microphone permission only when the user starts voice input.
Keep audio format handling explicit and match the session configuration.
Close subscriptions and audio resources when the session ends.

output_examples.input: Create a checklist for adding function calling to a voice assistant.
output: Define each function with a clear name, purpose, and required inputs.
Validate model-supplied arguments before calling external services.
Return concise function results to the conversation.
Trigger a follow-up response after the function result is added.

best_practices: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID or managed credentials over API keys when possible.
Handle connection, authentication, protocol, transcription, and audio events explicitly.
Close subscriptions and release microphone or audio resources after each session.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode Azure keys or tenant identifiers in browser code.
Do not ignore audio sample rates or format mismatches between client and service.
Do not leave Voice Live sessions open after the user ends the interaction.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build TypeScript applications that use Azure AI Voice Live for real-time voice interaction.

faq.question: Does it include a full application template?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance, examples, and review prompts for your own application.

faq.question: Can it help with browser projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers browser credential considerations, microphone access, and audio session concepts.

faq.question: Does it require Azure credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. You need an Azure AI resource and valid credentials for a working integration.

faq.question: Can it guide function calling?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes how to configure tools and return function results during a voice session.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
